_note: Faction doctrines (docs/developer/factions.md): the enemy factions' campaign and level data, and the player's own settlement (colony). Phase A steps the launcher mobility only; stockpile, conversion and the level fields come with later phases.
_intercept: Phase D (docs/developer/factions.md, Interception): a jump whose line passes within range of a faction ship in flight, or that arrives where a mothership (or a ship docked at it) is in orbit, meets it. Evading costs evade_fuel and fails with catch_chance (then the ship is boarded anyway); both are indexed by the ship's tier, the last entry a mothership's. Parley is offered only to a neutral faction.

hive._morphs: Until the player has learned the hive's shared identity (phase B+, LoreLinks), every player-facing name is the morph's, never the faction's. A site's morph comes from its scenario: morph_by_scenario, else default_morph. blueprint is the prefix of the morph's life-stage blueprints (<prefix>_egg, _hatchling, _stage2, _stage3, _egg_cracked).

mobility._spread: Fires at spread_share of the site's capacity (at least spread_min, at most the capacity). Below crowded_capacity the cooldown stretches by crowded_capacity / capacity and also runs from arrival, so a cramped hive fires rarely.

capacity._note: base + each archetype tag + the location kind, floored at min.

hive._hazard: Growth multiplier by the site's scenario id; negative shrinks the presence until it dies. Unlisted scenarios are 1.

stages.name: hive
stages._seen_name: DRAFT: the top stage's player-facing name (hidden identity: never "hive").

hive._research: The Tier 1 walk (abstract points): the spine keeps Phase A's costs and range positions (the brood unlocks where the tier entries stood: hive_plan.md, The evolve tree), so the launcher range grows on the same day; the rest follows. The live hive walks the same order at its evolution chamber (settlement.research).
hive._types: Unit types (hive_plan.md): the colour block is the type, applied at spawn by the factory (factory.ApplyType): sprite_dx on body and egg, the adult's absolute stats, role and tasks on a worker, skills and kit, the egg's hatch_turns, and seen_name as the body's name until the morph link is known (name after; B+). A type with unlock is raised only once that research is known; its share of a stage's mix goes to its morph's morph_fallback. tech_aliases map an old save's tier techs to the entries that replaced them.
hive._body_skills: Skills every typed body has at every life stage (egg, hatchling, adult): a hive lives where Tier 1 puts it, moons included, so its bodies shrug off a world's background radiation.
hive._settlement: The hive as a settlement (hive_plan.md): crew by type (the grow rung lays eggs on larvae; a settled egg's hatchling grows into the morph's crew body), biomass its only resource and its diet, its own build menu and evolve tree, larvae from the heart and egg clusters, kill drops (every corpse is biomass), a staged camp (the brood: heart, pool and a resin patch; the nest and hive stamps laid with resin).

hive._biomass: The abstract biomass tally (Tier 1; campaign/faction_hive.go): each drone forages per_drone a day (x 1 + tag per biomass tag of the site), each body eats eat, each new body spends its egg's cost; held between 0 and cap + per_pool per pool the director wants. Bookkeeping: it never blocks growth.
hive._conversion: Resin, the hive's creep: the share of the radius-14 patch round its centre laid with hive_resin (the director's resin rung live; Tier 1 accrues it at per_day x the population's share of capacity x the resin research). floor 1.0: resin does not cap capacity, so Tier 1 growth is Phase A's. No tags: a conversion tag would also weight seeding (economyWeight) and move every seed's hives.
hive._level: Materialising a presence on its level (factions.md, Tier 2): egg_share of the bodies are eggs, adult_share of the hatched ones adults (the rest stage 2); a stage's mix splits them by type (fighting types swapped with their other-morph counterparts on a site whose morph is not the default); the launcher stage stands a launcher; an exhausted presence leaves the husk stamp (cracked eggs).

greyish._instance_names: DRAFT: the names a second, third... faction of this doctrine takes in one campaign (rival_selection_plan.md, Names); shown where the faction is named openly (an observer run's Factions tab).
greyish._race: Phase F step 6 (playable_races_plan.md, greyish_plan.md "Phase F: what a greyish player will see"): a grey run is a ship run: the player flies a saucer with a grey crew (a worker, a technician and a soldier), and wins by reaching Home as the colony does. All text is draft.

race._text: DRAFT: the blurb is a placeholder for the owner.
race.blurb: A saucer and three greys, far from the mothership. Print a crew, grow the hull, and find the way Home.
race._start: A ship race's start (playable_races_plan.md, 6a): units are the crew by type, gear each type's kit, aboard the structures standing on the ship from the start (beside the hold), stockpile the hold. The scout's crew, armed as a scout's soldier is before beam weapons.

greyish._greyish: Phase D (docs/developer/factions.md, The greyish): a fleet faction that lands, salvages and leaves. Ships carry the presence (crew, hold, techs); a landed ship's crew mines and hauls into its hold, and once the hold reaches ships.hold_target the ship lifts off for the mothership, which hoards, raises ship tiers (crew caps) and builds new ships. Hostile from first contact (diplomacy). Seeded from the third rival faction on (seed_from).
greyish._types: Phase E4 (docs/brainstorm/greyish_plan.md, The roster): few bodies, each expensive and strong. Printed at the grey vat; the scout's three are a worker, a technician and a soldier. The lancer has no mix share (it comes from the emitter posts), so Tier 1's composition never names it. Names are drafts.
greyish._second_walk: Phase E4 (greyish_plan.md, Tier 1: two walks): a ship's second walk while landed, on the days the spine walks, per day by hull tier. Bookkeeping only: no entry changes a number Tier 1 reads.
greyish._raid: The raid rung counts armed soldiers, heavies and lancers, after contact (a skimmer's patrol, or the player at the camp), led by a heavy once heavies exist: a scout's one soldier never raids, a freighter's two do (phase E4).
greyish.raid_alert: {name} soldiers are moving on your colony on {place}.

ships._ships: tiers cap a ship's crew and rise only at the mothership, paid from its hoard; hold_target is the hold (units) at which a landed ship goes home; yield is a landed ship's abstract digging per crew member a day by site tag (base: every site).
ships._modules: Phase E4: what each hull carries and unpacks on landing (greyish_plan.md, Structures); an object's requires_tech gates it. Freighters and warships carry the armory once the armory module is known; a scout builds its own (the mothership's beam-down pays for it). Modules move no Tier 1 number.

mothership._beam: Phase E4 (the owner's call, 2026-11-12): the mothership keeps a stock apart from its hoard and beams it down to a camp on a loaded level, as the colonists beam from their ship: once a day the camp is topped up to the floor, from the stock, then the hoard. Tier 1 never beams, so the pace does not move.

settlement._ship: Phase F step 6c (greyish_plan.md, The saucer): a grey player's ship is a round hull, one deck of radius 8 to start (about 200 floor tiles, near the colony's starting grid of rooms). The rings and decks it grows by come with step 6d.
settlement._rings: Phase F step 6d (greyish_plan.md, The saucer; open question 17's defaults): rings 8 to 10 to 12 to 15 to 18, decks up to the level's four, each new deck at the start radius. The ring to 10 and the second deck need only materials; the others need the hull entries. Expand Hull and Add Deck queue the work as orders (a breach, the floor, the new rim, then the old rim dug out).
settlement._interface: Phase F step 6 (greyish_plan.md, The rest of the player's side): the colonist's modal less needs and sleep (no bed, no hunger), the crew panel by type. Labels are drafts.

interface._text: DRAFT: the labels are placeholders for the owner.
interface._hidden_research: Entries that act only for a rival grey ship, left off a grey player's research screen: Tractor Lock and Cloak (a rival ship's catch chance and range against the player's jump, Tier 3), Mothership Bulwark (a boarded rival mothership's emitters), Armory Module (a rival hull's armory; the player builds grey_armory with no tech). The owner decides whether each gets a player effect.

settlement._ground: Phase E4: structures built on the ground (each left as its wreck at lift-off); modules come with the hull (ships.tiers). The gear floor arms bodies a ship printed off-level (open question 12). Phase D bodies are adopted once: a crew blueprint becomes its crew entry's type, anything else (the old green miner) the type_fallback.

director._priorities: Phase E4 (greyish_plan.md, The director table): a lancer for each standing emitter once the lancer pattern is known (the owner's call, 2026-11-12; over the crew cap, which the crew fills first), print to the crew cap, mine, dig for ore (above the builds: ore lies deep on most sites, and a build waiting on metal must not hold the shaft up), haul loose things home (a kill's specimens, a spilled pocket), lockers, the armory when the stay allows and none is carried, alloy, plastic pressed from biomass (research and the array and emitters take it in place of most of their metal: the owner's call, 2026-11-12), research (technicians only), weapons and armour per soldier and heavy, arm them, guard; emitters with lancers posted and the array on long stays; hunt wildlife for specimens; skimmers patrol; raid after contact, led by a heavy once heavies exist. Spending rungs keep a fifth of the hold target in reserve (the plan said half; half leaves no room to print below a 30-unit hold target).

autonz._autonz: Phase E (docs/developer/factions.md, The autonz): planet-carried, converting. A presence converts its site (conversion: the share of its patch laid with blue wire), and the share is its economy: growth stops at ConvertCap (floor of the capacity plus the rest by the share of the cap converted), ore feeds the rate, research raises it and the signal range. From the hub stage it sends a signal (mobility signal) on its cooldown once it reaches the firing threshold of the site's full capacity or signal_conversion: a dormant presence of egg_pop on a site within range, asleep for wake_days, a single sleeper node on its level. A fully converted site stops growing and spends shot_pop on each signal. Hostile from first contact (diplomacy unset). Seeded from the fourth rival faction on (seed_from), so Rival factions 1 to 3 seed as before. One organism with the autonz_incursion scenario's swarm (home_scenarios, the same faction string).
autonz._types: Phase E3 (docs/brainstorm/autonz_plan.md): the unit types, one silhouette each on scifi_entities, steel at y 936 (the blueprint's row) and bronze one row down (tiers: a type prints bronze once its bronze entry is known, at spawn only). A locked type's share goes to its fallback (the fighters' to the enforcer, the workers' to the wire placer), so a stage with nothing unlocked keeps Phase E's mix. A shot takes wire placers, then relay drones (economy_types).
autonz._assimilation: Phase E3: a second Tier 1 walk beside the research spine, its own points per stage (node 1, hub 2), so the spine's range and rate days do not move; known techs are the union. No entry here has a range or conversion_rate.

rows.label: Or take over what the units do:

settlement._crew: Wire placers convert, mine and haul; enforcers guard (and raid). The stage's mix replaces these shares on the level (materialise and the grow rung).
settlement._research: Both Tier 1 walks interleaved, worked one at a time at the cogitator.
settlement._camp: staged: each stage's stamp is the camp (the node, then the hub over it); the settlement's storage inside is claimed and the fabricator placed by the centre.

director._priorities: Phase E3 (autonz_plan.md, The director table): wire placers first, then wire laid outward from the hub and each converter node, ore (and loose ferrite) home, a locker, the cogitator and its assimilation, digging for ore, enforcer guards; at the hub the Signal Core, a relay pylon deployed toward the nearest site, the foundry and its ferrite, converter nodes, defence pylons with a sentinel each; the rest printed by the stage's mix; on a ready day two placers walked into the core; seekers and spare relay drones on patrol; raids after contact, led by a warden once wardens are known.

rival._rival: Rival selection step 2 (rival_selection_plan.md): a rival colony is this doctrine run by another faction, as a rival hive is the hive doctrine. These are the fields it reads in place of the colony's (once the mirror doctrine): its name and badge, a fleet's mobility (a ship stays stay_days on a site, then lifts off for a free site within base_range at ship_speed units a day; it waits in orbit of a loaded site), the ore economy, its landing kit, and its seeding (from the second rival faction on). legacy_key keeps the mirror's place in seeding and its faction key in a count-seeded campaign, so a campaign seed seeds as it did; old saves' mirror is this view. Neutral to the player until the player lands on a site it holds (diplomacy), then hostile.
rival.name: Rival Colony
rival._objective: Its ships seek the gate and leave the galaxy (pregenerated_galaxy_plan.md, the gate; campaign/gate.go): before they know where it is they move inward from the rim every explore_stay days; a ship landed within sense_range of the gate learns it for its faction; then it flies the shortest route of stops in reach to the controls world, switches the gate on there (live: its director orders the controls repaired; off a loaded level, after switch_days, losing switch_loss crew), and flies to the lit gate and leaves.

colony.name: Colony
colony._instance_names: DRAFT: the names a second, third... faction of this doctrine takes in one campaign (rival_selection_plan.md, Names); shown where the faction is named openly (an observer run's Factions tab).
colony._colony: The player's own settlement (phase C0): the build menu, research tree, printer units and crew read from settlement below. It reproduces the game as it was before doctrines. Not seedable; no Tier 1 fields. A playable hive or greyish fills the same settlement block (phase F).

mobility._observer: In an observer run the expedition is a fleet-carried presence of this doctrine (campaign.AddExpeditionFleet): it jumps at ship_speed units a day (generation's jump_fuel_per_day, as the player's ship), anywhere its fuel reaches (base_range 0), and stay_days is the fallback hop the expedition table overrides.

colony._presence: The expedition presence's Tier 1 (observer runs): the mirror's numbers, so a colony nobody is viewing grows, researches and holds its camp as a rival colony does.
colony._morphs: The expedition presence's name on the Star Map and in Legends (observer runs): EXPEDITION, not the doctrine's name.
colony._expedition: Observer mode v2: the expedition director flies the ship (internal/director/expedition.go, campaign.DoctrineExpedition). Once every every_days days it makes one move: reinforce the colony in orbit (fewer than reinforce_below alive, up to reinforce_to), pack it up (pack_up_at or fewer alive and no crew aboard), beam the kit down once the colony has a locker, found a colony with found_crew on a site scoring at least found_score, or (after stay_days in orbit, with crew aboard) jump to the best site by score, never below fuel_reserve. An incident is answered by travelling there when the ship has crew and the jump costs at most incident_fuel; an interception by the first possible answer in encounter.

expedition._fleet: A rival ship flying by this table (the mirror's, expedition_from colony): fleet_fuel at launch and at most, fleet_refuel_per_day refined at its camp a landed day (plus any fuel in its stockpile), and it leaves before its stay_days hop only for a site in reach scoring fleet_move_margin better than staying (the jump's fuel counted), or when its crew is down to pack_up_at.

settlement._interface: Phase F step 2: the colony's HUD as it was before doctrines, declared (docs/developer/factions.md, "The interface block").
settlement._crew: SeedShipCrew's composition: the title screen's crew count is split by share, the remainder to the first entry.
settlement._build_menu: Build menu categories in order. Each lists the build.json entries of that category that are also in buildables, by order then name. The orders category's items are the cursor modes, bound in code.
settlement._research: research.json entries this settlement can research.
settlement._units: Crafting recipes that make a unit (the bio-printer's colonist, the Robot Workbench's robots). Units and recipes together are everything the crafting modals offer.
settlement._director: Phase C1: the director runs this settlement in observer mode (docs/developer/factions.md, The director). Priorities are a needs ladder walked in order; build, research and craft share max_open open orders, mine and haul run beside them.
